start.text: *Tan's alarm goes off at six. It's a song Tan hates, so that he has to get up to turn it off.*

wake_2.text: *Ulyn is on the couch, under a blanket that smells like Tan's laundry soap and not like home. His phone is under his cheek.*

wake_3.text: *There's a message from last night that he didn't answer.*

wake_4.speaker: Mom
wake_4.text: coming home tomorrow? i'm making khao man gai 🍗

wake_5.speaker: Ulyn
wake_5.text: It's my favorite. She knows it's my favorite. That's why she says it.
wake_5.cut: Anyway. Council at eight. Coffee first.

wake_cant_2.text: *The smiley face is worse than if she'd been angry.*

wake_come_2.text: *Two smiley faces. He puts the phone face down on the cushion and looks at the ceiling for a while.*

wake_tan_1.text: *Tan shuffles past in his boxers, making coffee.*

wake_tan_5.text: *Tan says it in exactly the same voice Ulyn uses on Kay. Ulyn throws a pillow at him.*

gate_1.text: *At the gate, Kay is standing very still, staring at Elysia and her friends like they're a TV he forgot to turn off.*

gate_2.speaker: Ulyn
gate_2.text: He looks terrible. Grey under the eyes. Hair still wet.

gate_3.speaker: Ulyn
gate_3.text: Cold shower again? Did his heater break? He'd never say.

gate_4.text: *Elysia turns around like she felt him there and waves. Kay waves back a full second too late, his arm stiff as a railway crossing.*

gate_5.speaker: Ulyn
gate_5.text: He waved like a robot. Good job, Kay.

gate_6.text: *Ulyn puts a hand on his back.*

gate_11.speaker: Ulyn
gate_11.text: Late-ish. That means two at the earliest.

gate_12.text: *The slides were due at eight. Bank sent a crying emoji to the group chat at 1:48. Ulyn saw it. He didn't answer, because he was doing his own part like a normal person.*

gate_13.speaker: Ulyn
gate_13.text: "You did their slides again, didn't you."

gate_14.speaker: Kay
gate_14.text: "They were busy. It was faster if I just did it."

gate_15.speaker: Ulyn
gate_15.text: The science poster. The English skit. Now Obama. They were busy every time.

gate_17.text: *He wants to say more. You're allowed to say no. You look like you haven't slept in a month. I'm worried.*

gate_18.text: *But Kay's face has already closed, the way it does. Like a shop pulling the shutter down.*

gate_19.speaker: Ulyn
gate_19.text: If I push, he'll just smile harder.

gate_20.speaker: Ulyn
gate_20.text: "Come on, leader. Don't be late to your own presentation."

pres_1.text: *History. Group 3 at the front of the room. A gap between each of them, about one person wide.*

pres_2.text: *Kay does the introduction in his presentation voice. Steady. Friendly. Exactly the right amount of teeth.*

pres_3.speaker: Ulyn
pres_3.text: To everyone else he looks perfectly fine.

pres_4.text: *Ulyn watches his eyes instead. They keep sliding across the room, landing on nothing.*

pres_5.speaker: Ulyn
pres_5.text: "Ulyn. I made the slides, so if they look good, you're welcome."

pres_6.text: *People laugh. Being funny is the easiest thing Ulyn knows how to do.*

pres_7.speaker: Bank
pres_7.text: "So Obama was... he was born in..."

pres_8.text: *Bank looks at his phone. Scrolls. Scrolls again. The silence gets long enough to hear the air conditioner.*

pres_9.speaker: Ulyn
pres_9.text: He never read it. He never even opened it.

pres_10.text: *Ulyn looks at Kay. Kay's face doesn't move, but {one thumb presses into the other palm, hard|NoticedKayThumb}.*

pres_11.speaker: Ulyn
pres_11.text: Let him blank, Kay. Just once. Let it be someone else's problem.

pres_12.speaker: Kay
pres_12.text: "—Hawaii, 1961. Sorry, I'll jump in, we split this part."

pres_14.text: *Kay knows every date. He wrote every line. Fern points at a slide she has clearly never seen before, and Kay steps in again, so smoothly it looks planned.*

pres_15.speaker: Teacher
pres_15.text: "Very well organized, group 3. Good teamwork, everyone."

pres_19.text: *Ulyn doesn't look at Bank or Fern. He looks at Kay, who is smiling at them with his whole face except his eyes.*

pres_20.text: *Back at their seats, Ulyn drops into the chair next to him.*

pres_21.speaker: Ulyn
pres_21.text: "Why didn't you just let him blank?"

pres_22.speaker: Kay
pres_22.text: "In front of everyone? That would've been mean."

pres_23.speaker: Ulyn
pres_23.text: "It would've been fair. You wrote his part. You wrote her part. And they get the same grade as you."

pres_24.speaker: Ulyn
pres_24.text: "Last semester it was the science poster. Before that, the English skit."

pres_25.text: *Some of the frustration in his chest is about Bank and Fern. More of it is about Kay. Most of it, if he were being honest, which he isn't, is about something else.*

choices.text: "You were digging your thumb into your hand up there."

pres_always_1.speaker: Kay
pres_always_1.text: "They just forgot. It's not a big deal."

pres_always_2.speaker: Ulyn
pres_always_2.text: "Right. They forgot. For the third time."

pres_worried_1.text: *It comes out quieter than he meant it to.*

pres_worried_2.text: *Kay blinks. For a second something moves behind his face. Then the shutter comes down again.*

pres_worried_3.speaker: Kay
pres_worried_3.text: "Don't be. I'm fine. They just forgot."

pres_thumb_1.text: *Kay looks down at his hand like it belongs to someone else.*

pres_thumb_5.text: *It's the most honest thing he's said all day. Ulyn puts it away with everything else he's noticed since March.*

pres_after_1.text: *Ulyn turns to face the front. He doesn't sound angry anymore. He can hear that in his own voice. Just tired.*

pres_after_2.speaker: Ulyn
pres_after_2.text: He's looking at me like he thinks I'm mad at him.

pres_after_3.speaker: Ulyn
pres_after_3.text: I'm not mad at you, idiot. I'm mad at—

pres_after_4.text: *He doesn't finish the thought. He's gotten good at not finishing that thought.*

lunch_2.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_2.text: "Hey, so... I can't eat with you today. My chemistry report's due tomorrow and I haven't started."

lunch_3b.text: *Kay says it to his tray. {He hasn't touched his fried rice|NoticedKayTray}.*

lunch_5.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_5.text: "You sure? I can put it off and just do it tonight."

lunch_6.text: *He means it. He'd be up until four, and he'd do it gladly, if Kay asked.*

lunch_7.text: *Kay looks at him for a long moment. A whole conversation seems to be happening behind his eyes, one Ulyn isn't invited to.*

lunch_8.speaker: Kay
lunch_8.text: "I'm good. Really. Don't worry about me."

lunch_9.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_9.text: Don't worry about me. I could make a list of every time he's said that, starting last April.

lunch_10.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_10.text: "...Okay. Save me a seat in class, then."

lunch_go_1.text: *He jogs toward the building. At the door he glances back. Kay is still standing there, watching him go.*

lunch_go_2.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_go_2.text: He looks like a kid at a bus stop.

lunch_sit_1.text: *He makes it three steps. Then he turns around and drops his bag on the seat.*

lunch_sit_4.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_sit_4.text: "Too late, I'm sitting. What are we eating?"

lunch_sit_5.text: *Kay's face does something complicated. Ulyn thinks some of it might be relief.*

lunch_sit_6.text: *After twenty minutes, Kay says to go, seriously, he'll survive. This time he almost sounds like he means it. So Ulyn goes.*

lunch_tray_1.text: *Ulyn drops his bag on the seat.*

lunch_tray_2.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_tray_2.text: "You haven't eaten anything. I'm not leaving till you eat half."

lunch_tray_5.text: *He isn't. He writes the chemistry report in his head the whole time. Kay eats half, slowly, like it's homework.*

lunch_tray_6.text: *It isn't a conversation. But it's twenty minutes of Kay not eating alone.*

lunch_window_1.text: *From the library's second floor, you can see the cafeteria. Ulyn isn't looking. He's doing his chemistry report.*

lunch_window_3.text: *Kay is in the pad kra pao line. Right behind him, hands behind her back, is Elysia. She says something. Kay goes red to his ears.*

lunch_window_4.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_window_4.text: Good. Someone's dragging him out of himself.

lunch_window_5.text: *Ten minutes later he looks again. Kay is sitting at Elysia's table by the window. With her friends.*

lunch_window_6.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_window_6.text: Kay voluntarily sat at a table of other humans? I'm teasing him about this until the end of time.

lunch_window_9.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_window_9.text: "Ohh? You saw Elysia, didn't you. Look at your face."

lunch_window_11.text: *For about five minutes, everything is fine.*

lunch_window_12.speaker: Teacher
lunch_window_12.text: "The most common way people kill a plant isn't forgetting about it. It's overwatering it. Giving it more than it can take."

lunch_window_13.text: *Ulyn glances over. Kay is staring at nothing.*

lunch_window_14.speaker: Ulyn
lunch_window_14.text: He waters the plants in his front yard every day. He told me once, back when he still told me things.

lunch_window_16.text: *Ulyn doesn't know why that thought makes his chest go tight. He writes "overwatering" in the margin of his notebook and draws a box around it.*

council_1.text: *After school, the student council room smells like whiteboard markers and somebody's fish ball noodles.*

council_2.speaker: Pim
council_2.text: "Sports day. I need someone to run equipment, schedules, and the volunteer roster. It's basically half of the whole thing."

council_3.text: *Nobody raises a hand. Everyone looks at the table.*

council_4.text: *Ulyn thinks about Tan's couch. Mom's khao man gai. The quiet in that house, so quiet you can hear the fridge from upstairs.*

council_5.speaker: Ulyn
council_5.text: Busy is good. Busy means you don't have to think.

choices.text: "Someone else should take this one. I've got a lot on."

council_take_2.text: *Pim writes ULYN across half the board in red. Everyone claps. Ulyn bows.*

council_take_3.text: *Being useful feels like a warm room.*

council_no_1.text: *The room goes quiet. Pim looks surprised.*

council_no_2.speaker: Pim
council_no_2.text: "...Okay. Fair. You've done a lot this year."

council_no_3.text: *She splits it three ways instead. It's the first time he's said no to anything in months. His hands are a little shaky. He doesn't know why.*

evening_2.text: *At Tan's, they eat instant noodles over the sink.*

evening_3.speaker: Tan
evening_3.text: "Your mom texted me, by the way. She asked if you're eating."

evening_home_1.text: *He goes home. Same shoes by the door, minus one pair.*

evening_home_2.text: *Mom has set three places at the table, then noticed, and moved one plate back to the cupboard. He can see the clean circle where it was.*

evening_home_5.text: *The khao man gai is perfect. They talk about the chicken for a long time, because the chicken is safe.*

evening_home_6.text: *On the balcony, her plants are brown. All of them.*

text_1.text: *10:47 p.m. Ulyn opens his chat with Kay.*

text_2.text: *He thinks about the morning. Late-ish. The thumb pressing into the palm. Don't worry about me.*

text_3.speaker: Ulyn
text_3.text: yo. you good? you seemed off today

text_4.text: *The reply comes fast. Too fast, like it was ready.*

text_5.speaker: Kay
text_5.text: yeah all good! just tired lol

text_6.speaker: Ulyn
text_6.text: Exclamation mark. "lol." That's his customer service voice.

text_9.text: *The {typing dots appear and disappear three times|NoticedTyping}. Ulyn sits up.*

text_10.speaker: Ulyn
text_10.text: Come on. Come on, say it.

choices.text: "ok. i'm here if you wanna talk. like whenever"
"you typed something three times. what was it?"

text_dots_3.speaker: Ulyn
text_dots_3.text: dumb is fine. i like dumb

text_dots_6.speaker: Ulyn
text_dots_6.text: Maybe tomorrow. It's the most he's given me since March.

march_2.speaker: Ulyn
march_2.text: I'm here if you wanna talk. As if he would. As if I've earned that.

march_3.text: *He scrolls up. Not far. He knows exactly where it is.*

march_8.text: *That week his dad carried boxes to a car. His mom ran the shower every night so he wouldn't hear her cry. He heard her anyway.*

march_9.text: *He sat on Tan's floor with the phone in his hand and thought: I can't. If he needs something, I don't have anything to give.*

march_10.text: *So he gave nothing. And four days later it felt too late to give anything real.*

march_11.text: *Kay never asked again. Not for a pen. Not for a ride. Not for a phone call.*

march_12.speaker: Ulyn
march_12.text: I broke something. I just don't know if he knows I know.

tue_1.text: *Tuesday. Lunch. He finished the chemistry report at three. He lies with his forehead flat against the table.*

tue_2.speaker: Ulyn
tue_2.text: "Finished the chemistry report at three. Don't look at me."

tue_3.text: *He feels Kay looking anyway. Neither of them says anything about three in the morning.*

tue_4.text: *Homeroom. The teacher writes COMMUNITY PROJECT on the board.*

tue_6.speaker: Ulyn
tue_6.text: "He's with me. You two can come, I guess."

tue_7.text: *While they argue about topics, Ulyn looks out the window. Four raised beds behind the science building, weeds as tall as a kid. He walks past them every morning from Tan's.*

tue_8.text: *He remembers Mom's balcony before March. Herbs. A lime tree in a big blue pot. Now it's brown sticks.*

tue_9.speaker: Ulyn
tue_9.text: Nobody was home to water them.

tue_10.speaker: Ulyn
tue_10.text: "The garden. The agriculture club died two years ago. Nobody's touched it since."

tue_11.text: *The teacher approves it. Fern says "aesthetic." Bank asks if gardening is physical. Yes, Bank. It's physical.*

tue_12.speaker: Fern
tue_12.text: "So you'll do the report and the plan, right? You're so good at that."

tue_13.text: *Bank nods like it's already decided. Ulyn's pen stops.*

tue_14.speaker: Ulyn
tue_14.text: Say no. Say no, say no, say—

choices.text: "We should split it. Everyone writes their own part."

tue_quiet_1.text: *He grips the pen and says nothing. Saying it in front of them would only embarrass Kay. That's what he tells himself.*

tue_split_2.speaker: Ulyn
tue_split_2.text: "I mean— it's a lot for one person."

tue_split_3.speaker: Kay
tue_split_3.text: "It's fine. I'm faster at it anyway."

tue_split_5.text: *So it doesn't change anything. But under the desk, Kay's thumb stops pressing into his palm. Just for a second.*

sat_1.text: *The first Saturday, Ulyn snoozes his alarm twice and gets to the garden at 8:20 with a bag of bread from 7-Eleven.*

sat_2.text: *Kay is already there. He has pulled out an entire bed of weeds by himself. Mud to the elbows.*

sat_7.text: *Ulyn hands him a bread roll and doesn't say anything else.*

sat_8.speaker: Ms. Noi
sat_8.text: "Water spinach is forgiving. Basil isn't. Chili sulks if you love it too much."

sat_11.speaker: Ms. Noi
sat_11.text: "Once a day. Only if the soil is dry."

sat_12.text: *Kay writes it down, word for word. Ulyn watches him underline "only."*

sat_13.speaker: Ulyn
sat_13.text: He's going to water them twice a day. I'd bet my lunch.

busy_1.text: *Sports day takes over his life. Spreadsheets. Rosters. A group chat with ninety people in it who all have questions.*

busy_2.text: *He sleeps at Tan's five nights a week, then six. When he makes it to the garden, the soil is always wet and the hose is always out.*

busy_4.text: *Mom calls every evening at seven. He watches it ring.*

busy_4b.speaker: Ulyn
busy_4b.text: She's probably sitting at the table right now. Same chair. Same quiet kitchen.
busy_4b.cut_after: She's probably sitting at the table
busy_4b.cut: Ninety unread in the group chat. Answer the chat.

busy_5.text: *The third Friday, he wakes up in history to the teacher saying his name. There's a crease on his forehead from the council folder.*

busy_7.text: *The class laughs. He did that. Good.*

busy_8.text: *After the bell, his phone buzzes on the desk. Mom.*

busy_8b.text: *He shoves it in his pocket, the way he always does.*

busy_9.text: *When he looks up, Kay is watching him.*

busy_12.text: *Tan asks if he's going home. Pim asks if the roster is done. Mom asks if he's eating. Nobody has asked are you okay.*

busy_13.speaker: Ulyn
busy_13.text: And it's Kay asking. Kay, who hasn't asked me for anything since March.
busy_13.cut: Doesn't matter. Roster's due at five.

busy_14.speaker: Ulyn
busy_14.text: Did he see the call? Did he see who it was?

busy_fine_3.text: *Kay looks at him a beat too long, then nods.*

busy_fine_4.text: *Ulyn has the uncomfortable feeling he just did something very familiar. He can't place it.*

busy_honest_1.text: *He immediately wants to take it back. Kay goes very still.*

busy_honest_3.speaker: Ulyn
busy_honest_3.text: "My mom keeps calling. I keep not answering. Long story."

busy_honest_4.speaker: Kay
busy_honest_4.text: "...You can tell me. If you want."

busy_honest_6.text: *The bell rings. Saved by it. He doesn't tell him later. But Kay's face, saying "you can tell me," stays with him all day.*

seven_1.text: *At 7 p.m. the phone rings again. Mom.*

seven_decline_1.text: *He declines it. Then he sits on Tan's balcony with the phone in his hand for an hour, which is somehow worse than answering.*

seven_answer_2.speaker: Mom
seven_answer_2.text: "Oh! Hi. Hi, Ulyn. I just— are you eating?"

seven_answer_4.speaker: Mom
seven_answer_4.text: "Good. Good. I just wanted to hear your voice."

seven_answer_5.text: *He doesn't know what to say to that, so he talks about sports day for fifteen minutes. She listens to every word.*

sports_2.text: *Ulyn runs it with a clipboard and a megaphone he doesn't really need. The relay starts on time. The rope arrives. Nobody faints. Pim hugs him.*

sports_3.text: *It feels like a warm room again. He tries to stay in it.*

sports_4.text: *At the water station, Kay is filling paper cups. Ulyn didn't ask him to volunteer. Of course he volunteered. He looks grey, the way old newspaper is grey.*

sports_5.speaker: Ulyn
sports_5.text: He looks like he hasn't slept since the Obama presentation.

sports_6.text: *Elysia runs up to the station, pushes a cold drink into Kay's hands, and sprints away before her friends can catch her. Kay holds it like it's made of glass.*

sports_7.text: *At 2 p.m., Ulyn sees his mom in the stands. Work clothes. She must have taken the afternoon off. She waves. Small. Unsure.*

sports_9.text: *Pim is shouting about the closing ceremony. Ninety people need things.*

choices.text: Hold up the clipboard. "Too busy. Later."
Hand the megaphone to Pim and go up to her

sports_busy_1.text: *He points at the clipboard and mouths: busy, sorry, later. She nods and smiles, like she expected it.*

sports_busy_2.text: *At five, there's a container of khao man gai on the council table with a sticky note: "Proud of you. Eat something. - Mom"*

sports_busy_3.text: *He eats it alone behind the gym, on an upside-down crate. It's perfect. It tastes like the kitchen before March.*

sports_busy_4.text: *He doesn't cry. He's very busy not crying.*

sports_mom_4.text: *He climbs the stands. Mom looks startled, then happy, then like she's trying not to look too happy in case it scares him off.*

sports_mom_5.speaker: Mom
sports_mom_5.text: "I brought khao man gai. It's in the car. I didn't know if you'd—"

sports_mom_7.text: *They watch the relay for five minutes. She doesn't ask when he's coming home. He's grateful for that, and a little disappointed.*

mid_1.text: *Week five. Midterms. 1 a.m. at Tan's kitchen counter. Tan comes out for water.*

mid_after_1.speaker: Tan
mid_after_1.text: "You said that before the last exams."

mid_after_2.speaker: Ulyn
mid_after_2.text: "Then I'll say it again before the next ones."

mid_after_3.text: *Tan doesn't laugh. He fills his glass and goes back to bed.*

mid_honest_1.text: *Tan stops with the glass halfway to his mouth.*

mid_honest_2.speaker: Ulyn
mid_honest_2.text: "It's so quiet there. She tries so hard. She sets three plates and then moves one. I don't know how to be in that kitchen."

mid_honest_3.text: *Tan sits down on the other stool.*

mid_honest_4.speaker: Tan
mid_honest_4.text: "When my parents split, I lived at the 24-hour McDonald's for a month."

mid_honest_6.speaker: Tan
mid_honest_6.text: "Didn't fix anything. Just made me fat. You can stay here as long as you want. But you know you can't stay here forever."

mid_text_2.speaker: Ulyn
mid_text_2.text: u alive? midterms are killing me

mid_text_4.speaker: Ulyn
mid_text_4.text: Exclamation mark. Flexing emoji. Kay does not use emojis. Kay uses periods.

mid_text_5.text: *He types "can I call you." He looks at it.*

mid_text_8.text: *Thursday night, he falls asleep at 11 with the light on.*

where_1.text: *The sixth Thursday. Kay isn't at the gate. Kay isn't in homeroom.*

where_2.speaker: Ulyn
where_2.text: Kay is never late. He came in with a fever in tenth grade and threw up in the bin by the stairs and then sat through math.

where_3.speaker: Ulyn
where_3.text: where are u. ur never late

where_5.text: *He checks his phone under the desk eleven times in chemistry.*

where_6.speaker: Ulyn
where_6.text: He'd answer if he was just sick. He'd say "just a cold! don't worry!" with an exclamation mark.

where_7.text: *At lunch, before he can sit down, Elysia is standing at the end of his table. No friends. Not smiling. It's like seeing a teacher in a supermarket.*

where_8.speaker: Elysia
where_8.text: "Can I talk to you? Just for a second."

where_10.speaker: Elysia
where_10.text: "Kay texted me this morning. He said he couldn't get up."

where_11.text: *She chooses the next words carefully, like putting a cup on a table that might wobble.*

where_14.speaker: Elysia
where_14.text: "He asked me to leave him alone for now. So I am. I want to respect that."

where_15.speaker: Elysia
where_15.text: "But you're... different. You're Ulyn. He talks about you like..."

where_17.speaker: Elysia
where_17.text: "Could you go see him? After school?"

where_18.speaker: Ulyn
where_18.text: He talks about me like what?

where_20.speaker: Elysia
where_20.text: "Don't tell him I asked you. He'll think he's a bother."

where_21.text: *The council has the sports day wrap-up at 3:30. Ulyn is supposed to present the volunteer report. He finds Pim in the hallway.*

choices.text: "I've got a stomachache. Can you present it?"
"I can't today. My best friend needs me."

where_lie_3.text: *The voice in his head sounds a lot like his own.*

where_true_1.text: *Pim looks at him. Something in his face makes it serious. She just takes the folder.*

where_true_3.text: *It's that easy. He doesn't know why he thought it wouldn't be.*

shop_1.text: *Crispy pork from the stall by school. Two cartons of pink milk.*

shop_2.text: *Then, without deciding to, he grabs the cheap coconut cookies from the bottom shelf.*

shop_3.speaker: Ulyn
shop_3.text: He ate these every single day in tenth grade. One at a time, slowly, like they were expensive. I haven't seen him eat one since March.

step_1.text: *4:10. He knocks. It takes a long time. Then the door opens.*

step_2.text: *Kay is in a T-shirt with sleep lines on his face. Smaller than at school, like the uniform was holding him up.*

step_6.text: *They sit on the front step. Kay doesn't invite him in. Ulyn doesn't ask. The plants in the yard have yellow leaves and soil so wet it shines.*

step_7.speaker: Ulyn
step_7.text: "Your plants look worse than our garden."

step_10.text: *Kay sees the coconut cookies. His face does something very small. Ulyn isn't sure what it is.*

step_11.speaker: Ulyn
step_11.text: "You weren't at school. You're never not at school. You came in with a fever in tenth grade. You threw up in the bin by the stairs and then sat through math."

step_13.text: *Ulyn has rehearsed this for a year. In his head it always comes out clean. It doesn't come out clean.*

step_14.speaker: Ulyn
step_14.text: "Can I say something? You don't have to say anything back."

step_16.speaker: Ulyn
step_16.text: "Last year. March. You messaged me at like three in the morning. 'Can I call you.'"

step_17.speaker: Ulyn
step_17.text: "I saw it. And I didn't answer for four days. And then I said, 'sorry, was busy.'"

step_18.text: *He tells him the rest. His dad's boxes. The shower running. Tan's floor. I don't have anything to give. The worst possible thing, four days late.*

step_19.speaker: Ulyn
step_19.text: "And you never asked me for anything again. Not even 'can I call you.'"

step_20.speaker: Ulyn
step_20.text: "I've been waiting a whole year for you to try again so I could do it right. And you just got really, really good at being fine."

step_21.text: *Kay is quiet for a long time.*

step_22.speaker: Kay
step_22.text: "It's fine. It was a long time ago."

step_25.speaker: Kay
step_25.text: "Really. You had your own stuff going on."

step_26.text: *He could let it go. Eat the pork. Watch the streetlights come on. Kay would be relieved. Ulyn knows how to give people what they want.*

step_okay_3.speaker: Ulyn
step_okay_3.text: Relief. Or giving up. I can't tell. I never could.

step_okay_4.text: *They eat the crispy pork in silence. The streetlights come on. At the gate, Ulyn stops.*

step_okay_8.text: *He stops outside a closed bakery on the way and stands there for ten minutes, not crying.*

step_push_2.text: *Kay looks at him for a long time. Ulyn holds still, like you would near a bird.*

step_push_5.speaker: Kay
step_push_5.text: "Not just for you. When my dad left, I was twelve. Mom cried at the kitchen table for like a month."

step_push_7.speaker: Ulyn
step_push_7.text: Two years. I've eaten his mom's food. Slept on his floor after horror movies. I knew his dad wasn't around. I never asked. He never said.

step_push_9.speaker: Kay
step_push_9.text: "And I decided I'd just be easy. The kid who doesn't need anything. And when you didn't answer, I thought, yeah. That's right. That's what happens when I ask."

step_push_11.speaker: Kay
step_push_11.text: "And this year it's been... It's like everything's far away. I wake up and I already want the day to be over."

step_push_12.speaker: Kay
step_push_12.text: "Some nights I think everyone would be fine without me. Not like— I'm not going to do anything. I just think it. Like it's a fact."

step_push_13.text: *Something cold goes all the way through him, like swallowing ice. Every part of him wants to grab Kay by the shoulders.*

choices.text: Breathe first. "It's not a fact. And thank you for telling me."

step_panic_2.text: *Kay flinches. The shutter starts to come down. Ulyn can see it happening.*

step_panic_3.speaker: Kay
step_panic_3.text: "Forget it. I didn't mean it like— forget it."

step_panic_5.speaker: Ulyn
step_panic_5.text: "No— sorry. Sorry. I panicked. I'm listening. I'm here. Please don't forget it."

step_panic_8.text: *The shutter stays halfway up. Ulyn decides that's enough to work with.*

step_panic_9.speaker: Ulyn
step_panic_9.text: "It's not a fact. And I'm glad you told me."

step_calm_1.text: *He breathes in. Out. He picks the words one at a time, like stepping stones.*

step_calm_2.speaker: Ulyn
step_calm_2.text: "It's not a fact. And thank you for telling me. I mean it."

step_calm_4.speaker: Ulyn
step_calm_4.text: He expected me to freak out. I am freaking out. Just very quietly.

step_ask_1.speaker: Ulyn
step_ask_1.text: "But I'm not okay with you thinking that alone. Will you talk to someone? Someone who actually knows what to do. Not just me throwing pork at you."

step_ask_2.speaker: Ulyn
step_ask_2.text: "Ms. Noi runs the guidance room on Thursdays. My cousin went to something like that last year. It helped him."

step_ask_3.speaker: Ulyn
step_ask_3.text: Tan never talks about it. He told me once, at two in the morning.

step_ask_4.text: *Kay doesn't answer yet. Ulyn doesn't make him.*

step_ask_5.speaker: Ulyn
step_ask_5.text: "And you're not too much. You were never too much. I was too little, that week. That's different."

step_ask_6.text: *Kay's eyes go wet. He cries quietly, like he's had practice. That's the worst part.*

step_ask_7.text: *Ulyn looks at the road and pushes the second carton of pink milk into his hand.*

step_ask_8.text: *The silence is different now. Not the silence of not saying things. The silence after saying them.*

step_ask_9.text: *Ulyn thinks about the phone in his pocket. Mom. Seven o'clock, every night.*

choices.text: "I'm not okay either, by the way."
Keep it to yourself. Tonight is about Kay.

step_admit_1.speaker: Ulyn
step_admit_1.text: "I'm not okay either, by the way. I don't go home if I can help it. That's why I'm on every committee in this school."

step_admit_4.speaker: Kay
step_admit_4.text: "You decline your mom's calls in class."

step_admit_6.speaker: Ulyn
step_admit_6.text: He saw. All this time I was watching him so carefully, and he was watching me back.

step_admit_8.text: *They both laugh. Small and tired, but real.*

step_keep_1.text: *He doesn't say it. Tonight is Kay's.*

step_keep_2.text: *But Kay looks over at him, just once, the way he did that Friday in history. Like he's checking.*

step_keep_4.text: *Ulyn doesn't know how Kay knows to ask that.*

bus_2.speaker: Ulyn
bus_2.text: i went. he says he's fine.

bus_5.text: *He doesn't answer for a long time.*

bus_ok_1.speaker: Ulyn
bus_ok_1.text: he's ok. ish. thanks for telling me.

bus_ok_2.text: *She replies with one heart. Nothing else.*

bus_ok_3.speaker: Ulyn
bus_ok_3.text: She's crying. Or she's in class. No, it's seven. She's crying.

bus_wait_1.text: *The bus to Tan's is number 8. The bus home is number 21.*

bus_home_1.text: *The house is dark except for the kitchen.*

bus_home_2.text: *Mom is sitting at the table in her work clothes, doing nothing. When the door opens she turns around fast, like a deer.*

bus_home_5.speaker: Mom
bus_home_5.text: "You didn't say you were— I don't have anything. There's leftover khao man gai, from Sunday, I can heat it—"

bus_home_7.text: *They eat it standing at the counter, out of the container, with two forks.*

bus_home_8.speaker: Ulyn
bus_home_8.text: "Kay wasn't at school today. He's not doing good."

bus_home_15.text: *He looks at the third chair. The one nobody sits in.*

bus_home_17.text: *It's the second time today. It's easier the second time.*

bus_home_18.text: *She doesn't cry. She just squeezes his wrist across the counter, and they finish the container together.*

bus_home_19.text: *He sleeps in his own bed. The house is very quiet. He can hear the fridge from upstairs.*

bus_home_20.speaker: Ulyn
bus_home_20.text: It's okay. It's just a fridge.

bus_tan_1.text: *21 pulls up. The doors open. The driver looks at him.*

bus_tan_3.text: *At Tan's, he lies on the couch and looks at the ceiling. His phone buzzes at nine. Mom.*

gate2_1.text: *The next Monday, from the top of the stairs, Ulyn watches Kay walk straight across the front of the school to Elysia and her friends. In front of everybody.*

gate2_2.speaker: Elysia
gate2_2.text: "Yes, he's my boyfriend, we all know, moving on."

gate2_3.text: *She grabs Kay's hand. Kay turns the color of a chili.*

gate2_4.speaker: Ulyn
gate2_4.text: Whatever happened on Saturday, I'm taking partial credit.

gate2_6.text: *At lunch, Kay is standing in front of the guidance room door. Just standing there.*

gate2_8.text: *Kay knocks. The door opens. He goes in. Ulyn lets out a breath he didn't know he was holding.*

thu_walk_1.text: *Ulyn walks Kay to the guidance room. Kay holds the strap of his bag with both hands the whole way.*

thu_walk_2.speaker: Ulyn
thu_walk_2.text: "I'll be in the cafeteria. If you come out in thirty seconds, I'm sending you back in."

thu_walk_3.text: *Kay looks at him. Then he knocks.*

thu_walk_4.text: *Ulyn waits in the cafeteria for forty minutes, watching the hallway. Kay doesn't come out.*

thu_walk_5.speaker: Ulyn
thu_walk_5.text: Good. That's good. Stay in there.

noi_1.text: *When the bell rings, Ms. Noi is standing in the hallway by the home ec room. Looking at him.*

noi_3.speaker: Ulyn
noi_3.text: "I don't know what you're talking about."

noi_5.text: *It's the second time this semester someone has asked him that and waited for the answer.*

noi_fine_1.speaker: Ulyn
noi_fine_1.text: "Fine! Great. Busy. You know. Sports day."

noi_fine_2.text: *Sports day was three weeks ago. Ms. Noi nods like she believes him. She doesn't.*

noi_ask_1.text: *His mouth says it before his brain approves it. Ms. Noi doesn't look surprised.*

noi_ask_2.speaker: Ms. Noi
noi_ask_2.text: "The slot after Kay's is free. Come with an empty stomach. I make too much tea."

group_1.text: *Two weeks before the presentation, the group meets at the garden. Water spinach gone feral. Marigolds. Three small chilies, which Ulyn has named.*

group_2.speaker: Fern
group_2.text: "Okay, so Kay. You'll put the presentation together like last time? You're the fastest."

group_4.text: *Ulyn looks at Kay. Kay is looking at the soil.*

group_5.speaker: Ulyn
group_5.text: He's not doing it all again. Not this time. I could just say it.

group_wait_1.text: *Ulyn closes his mouth. He looks at Kay and waits.*

group_wait_3.text: *Kay looks up and sees him waiting. Something in his face changes.*

group_wait_4.speaker: Kay
group_wait_4.text: "I can't do all of it this time. I need everyone to do their own part."

group_wait_6.speaker: Bank
group_wait_6.text: "Oh. Wait. Did you... not want to? Before?"

group_wait_7.speaker: Kay
group_wait_7.text: "I offered because I didn't know how not to."

group_wait_8.text: *Ulyn has to look away so nobody sees his face.*

group_say_1.speaker: Ulyn
group_say_1.text: "He did the slides at 2:30 in the morning. And the poster. And the skit. So no."

group_say_2.text: *Bank and Fern agree, embarrassed, and start dividing things up. It works.*

group_say_3.text: *But Kay is quiet for the rest of the meeting. When Ulyn glances at him, he looks almost disappointed. Like Ulyn said his line before he could.*

group_say_4.speaker: Ulyn
group_say_4.text: Oh. That was his to say.

group_end_1.text: *Bank finds the old club photo album. Fern takes the slides.*

group_end_2.speaker: Ulyn
group_end_2.text: "And I'll do the budget. And stop sleeping in class. Maybe."

group_end_3.text: *That night there are four cursors in the shared document. Kay's cursor sits in the corner, not moving. He's just reading what the others wrote.*

sun_2.text: *He's still mostly at Tan's. Mom still calls at seven. Sometimes he answers. Sometimes he watches it ring.*

sun_home_1.text: *He goes home for dinner every Friday now. Some Fridays he stays until Sunday.*

sun_home_2.text: *Mom has bought a new lime tree for the balcony. It's small. She's very nervous about it.*

dad_2.text: *He hasn't picked up a call from his dad since April. They text on birthdays. Happy birthday son. Thanks.*

dad_answer_2.speaker: Dad
dad_answer_2.text: "Ulyn! Hi. Hi. I didn't think you'd— How's school?"

dad_answer_4.speaker: Dad
dad_answer_4.text: "A garden! Your mom always had the green thumb."

dad_answer_6.text: *It lasts four minutes. It's terribly awkward. It's four minutes more than last month.*

dad_ring_1.text: *It rings out. A text comes after.*

dad_ring_2.speaker: Dad
dad_ring_2.text: just wanted to say hi. proud of u.

dad_ring_3.text: *He doesn't reply. He doesn't delete it either.*

pres2_2.speaker: Ulyn
pres2_2.text: "Ulyn. I did the budget, so if it looks cheap, that's on purpose."

pres2_4.speaker: Bank
pres2_4.text: "So, the garden was first built in... in, uh..."

pres2_6.text: *Ulyn glances at Kay. Every muscle in Kay's body is ready to jump in.*

pres2_7.text: *Kay doesn't. He waits. He gives Bank a tiny nod.*

pres2_8.speaker: Bank
pres2_8.text: "Two thousand nine! The agriculture club. My uncle was actually in it. That's him, in the yellow boots."

pres2_9.speaker: Teacher
pres2_9.text: "Very well done, group 3. Good teamwork, everyone."

pres2_10.text: *Ulyn looks at Bank. At Fern. At Kay. Kay is smiling, and his eyes are in it too.*

last_1.text: *Friday. The last day of the semester.*

last_2.text: *At the gate, Elysia is showing her friends a picture of a huge beetle. Ulyn has no idea why. She's beaming.*

last_3.text: *Kay is next to her. He looks...*

last_5.speaker: Ulyn
last_5.text: Not like a zombie. Not grey. Not like old newspaper.

last_9.text: *The ninety-person group chat. Tan's couch. The third chair. Bus number 21.*

choices.text: "...My mom wants me to come home more. I'm trying."

last_true_1.speaker: Ulyn
last_true_1.text: "...My mom wants me to come home more. I'm trying."

last_true_2.text: *He scratches the back of his neck.*

last_true_4.speaker: Kay
last_true_4.text: "Want company? I can come over and be boring at your house."

last_true_5.text: *Kay is offering. Kay, who hasn't asked anyone for anything in a year, is offering to come sit in the quietest house in the city.*

last_busy_1.speaker: Ulyn
last_busy_1.text: "Good! Great! Busy! Next semester Pim wants me on the—"

last_busy_2.text: *Kay is looking at him with an expression Ulyn recognizes. He's worn it himself, watching Kay say "it's fine."*

last_busy_6.text: *Ulyn laughs, caught. He doesn't answer. But he doesn't change the subject either.*

endA_3.speaker: Ulyn
endA_3.text: come over? my mom's making khao man gai. she'd like it. i'd like it.

endA_4.text: *He sends it before he can delete it. It's the first thing he's asked Kay for in a year.*

endA_lunch_1.text: *Kay comes over. Mom makes khao man gai for three. She sets three plates. Nobody has to move one back.*

endA_lunch_2.text: *Kay eats slowly, the way he used to eat the coconut cookies. Mom watches him and looks happier than Ulyn has seen her since before March.*

endA_lunch_3.text: *After lunch, Kay walks out onto the balcony and looks at the brown sticks in their pots, and at the little new lime tree.*

endA_lunch_6.text: *Kay nods like that makes sense to him. They spend the afternoon pulling out the dead plants and repotting basil cuttings from the school garden.*

endA_lunch_7.text: *Kay pushes his finger into each pot.*

endA_lunch_8.speaker: Kay
endA_lunch_8.text: "Once a day. Only if it's dry."

endA_noi_1.text: *On Thursdays, Ulyn has the slot after Kay's. They pass each other in the doorway. Neither of them makes it weird. Ms. Noi makes too much tea.*

endA_call_1.text: *On Sunday his dad calls. Ulyn picks up. Six minutes, this time.*

endA_night_1.text: *Ulyn sleeps in his own bed. He can hear the fridge from upstairs, and Mom humming in the kitchen.*

endA_night_2.text: *It isn't the house before March. It's a different house. It's still home.*

endB_1.text: *He doesn't go home every night. Most nights, though.*

endB_2.speaker: Tan
endB_2.text: "Most nights is a lot better than no nights."

endB_3.text: *Tan says it while helping him carry half his things back on a Sunday.*

endB_porch_1.text: *Mom stops asking if he's coming. She just leaves the porch light on.*

endB_garden_1.text: *After school, he and Kay sit by the garden while Kay waters it. Almost exactly the right amount.*

endB_garden_10.text: *A thumbs up. From Kay, who doesn't use emojis.*

endB_garden_11.text: *Ulyn laughs alone in his room, in his own house, and doesn't feel like he has to explain it to anyone.*

endC_1.text: *Next semester, Pim wants him on student council, sports day, the welcome committee, and the yearbook. He says yes to all of it.*

endC_2.speaker: Pim
endC_2.text: "You're amazing. Seriously, what would we do without you?"

endC_3.text: *He sleeps at Tan's. Mom calls at seven. He watches it ring.*

endC_4.text: *Kay is still Kay. Steady. Smiling. A pause before every "fine." Ulyn still watches him from the next seat. Neither of them says anything.*

endC_kay_1.text: *Kay is doing better. Thursdays, the garden, Elysia holding his hand at the gate. Ulyn helped do that. He's sure he did.*

endC_kay_2.text: *He's glad. He's so glad it hurts a little. Somewhere along the way he got so busy watching Kay get better that he forgot to.*

endC_msg_1.text: *11:40 p.m. Tan's couch. His phone buzzes. Kay.*

endC_msg_4.text: *He looks at it. The exclamation mark. He knows exactly whose exclamation mark that is.*

endC_msg_8.text: *The message sits there. The cursor blinks. It's still his to send.*
